Care allowance, benefits in kind or both?
Depending on who provides the care, you are entitled to different benefits from the long-term care insurance fund. We help you make the most of it.
When loved ones provide the care, the long-term care insurance fund pays the care allowance directly to you – to use freely.

Good care begins with prevention. We explain the most important measures in plain terms – so that you can safely support your loved ones at home. When in doubt, we are happy to advise you in person.
Falls are one of the most common causes of hospital stays in old age. With a few measures you can reduce the risk considerably.
Remove trip hazards (loose rugs, cables, door thresholds)
Ensure good lighting – especially at night and in the bathroom
Fit grab rails in the bathroom, hallway and by the bed
Sturdy, non-slip footwear instead of slippers
Train strength and balance through gentle exercise
Pain reduces quality of life and mobility. It deserves to be recognised, taken seriously and treated in a targeted way.
Ask about pain regularly and document it
Give medication according to the doctor's plan and timing
In addition: heat/cold, gentle positioning, movement
Inform the doctor about new or stronger pain
Pressure ulcers develop when pressure acts on the same area of skin for a long time. Prevention is crucial here.
Change position regularly – according to individual need, often around every 2 hours
Keep the skin clean, dry and well cared for
Recognise early warning signs: redness that does not fade under finger pressure
Pay attention to a balanced diet and fluids
Especially in the case of being bedridden, the risk of pneumonia increases. Breathing and mobilisation provide protection.
Encourage breathing exercises and conscious deep breathing
Support an upright position (upper body raised)
Drink sufficiently, where permitted by the doctor
Tested standards – delivered close to people
Following the kinaesthetics concept, we support movement sequences individually – so independence is preserved and mobilisation succeeds more gently for both sides.
Use a person's existing movement rather than just „lifting"
Shape movement sequences together and individually
Shift weight over the body's masses (head, chest, pelvis)
Stiffening of the joints can be prevented through regular movement – important in cases of limited mobility.
Physiological positioning in a functional position
Motivate and guide towards independent movement
Use positioning aids in a targeted way
These tips do not replace medical advice. In the case of specific complaints or changes, please contact the treating doctor – or speak to us directly.
